dese_rule: Function 2110 is reported by program, and it holds the supervisor of pupil personnel and the special education administrators (EPIMS job codes 1211, 1212 and 1312).
why: The district's End of Year Report puts this one salary in the special education column in both years, to the dollar, and its budget book labels the line (Spec Ed). Every rule counts it.

item: "Spcl Ed" and "Spec Ed" in the budget book
dese_rule: DESE counts special education by program, whatever a line is called.
why: The budget model read "special ed" and "specl ed" only, so three lines the district labels special education were missed: contracted related services, special education supplies and the coordinator. The ledger rules already counted the first two.

dese_rule: DESE splits psychologists by EPIMS job code, special education (3361) or not (3360), and puts school social workers in the same function.
why: The district's two reports disagree. FY2023 puts every psychologist account and the testing materials in special education; FY2024 puts the same accounts in regular day and prints a separate special education figure that no FY2024 account holds. DESE's rule turns on a job code the ledger does not carry, so it is left out of every total and shown beside it.

dese_rule: DESE counts adjustment counselors coded special education (3351), not guidance counselors (3329) or other adjustment counselors (3350).
why: The report's special education share of guidance is the same figure in both years and matches no account. No ledger account says which counselor is coded special education, so none is counted.

dese_rule: DESE's chart gives Equipment (7300, 7400) no program: it is never special education. An item under $5,000 is not a 7000-series cost at all.
why: The report files equipment as undistributed, with no special education cell, and the form gives it none. Left out of every total.

item: School choice and charter school tuition (9110 and 9120)
dese_rule: DESE counts the special education part of both, as spending by the city or town, and records it by placement.
why: Counted by DESE, but as the town's spending: the state assesses it on the town and no school account carries it. Our rules measure school spending, so DESE's school committee total is the like-for-like comparison and this is shown beside it.

item: DESE's special education share of mixed instructional functions: teaching, aides, substitutes, therapy, supervision, supplies
dese_rule: These functions are split by program; a special education teacher, aide or substitute is reported under the special education program, whatever account pays them.
why: Our rules count the accounts the ledger names special education (teachers in town code 2310, aides, substitutes, therapists). DESE's figures are the district's allocation function by function, and which accounts make them up is in neither the report nor the ledger, so nothing further is added. Function by function they do not tie; the group totals are compared.

item: English learner accounts in the special education segment
dese_rule: English learner programs are reported as regular day, not special education.
why: Both accounts sit in segment 51, and the district's budget book labels them ELL (District Wide Specials (ELL), ELL General Supplies). Every rule leaves them out.

dese_rule: Special education is instruction under MGL c.71B and 603 CMR 28.00; a Section 504 plan is not.
why: In segment 51 and in the budget book's special education group, but a 504 plan is a general education accommodation. Every rule leaves it out.
